- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or near-zero — add 1–3% to forecast to compensate for bearish bias.
- Lagged forecasts tend to overreact to recent highs — adjust by smoothing the 30d forecast with a 7-day moving average to reduce overshoot.
- If sentiment is volatile (rapid swings > ±0.3), reduce forecast volatility by 15–20% to avoid overfitting to noise.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30d horizon, avoid forecasting sharp reversals unless sentiment confirms strong directional bias — cap extreme swings at ±5% of recent 14-day range.
